title: unified-rollouts-probing-weighted-canary-autorollback-workflow
author: Samantha Lee
description: Introduce a probing weighted-canary + staged shadow autorollback workflow for the unified rollouts controller. Motivation: current canary/AB workflows do not cover cases where model regressions are intermittent across traffic slices; combining lightweight probing with weighted canaries and staged shadow probing reduces blast radius while detecting regressions earlier. This PR implements the control-plane pieces for: 1) a new ProbingStage (CRD extension) that schedules short synthetic probe jobs against candidate model variants; 2) Weighted canary traffic step that increments traffic by configurable weights and waits for probe + production metrics to match expectations; 3) Shadow probing integration where a subset of traffic is identically mirrored to the candidate and probed in parallel; 4) Autorollback engine hooks that evaluate composite metrics (latency, error-rate, semantic-regression score) and trigger rollback if thresholds are breached; 5) observability additions: rollout-level telemetry, new histogram tags, and a sandbox dashboard. Implementation notes: - Feature gated behind rollout.experimental.probingWeightedCanary = true. Default: off. - New API surface: Rollout.spec.strategy.probingWeightedCanary and Rollout.status.probingStages[]. - Probing jobs are short-lived k8s Jobs that report a ProbeResult to the controller via the existing metrics ingestion API. - Autorollback now supports metric quorums: a configurable fraction of probes + production checks must pass. - Backwards compatible: existing canary/ab/shadow behaviors remain unchanged when the feature flag is unset. Migration: controller accepts both old and new rollout specs; CI includes an upgrade e2e that deploys an older Rollout spec and upgrades to the new controller to validate compatibility. Risks and mitigations: 1) Increased control-plane load from probes — probes are rate-limited and use shared worker pools; added circuit-breaker metrics. 2) False positives from probes — configurable quorum and multiple metric types reduce churn. 3) Observability noise — probe telemetry uses its own tag to separate from user metrics. Tests: unit tests for probe scheduling, integration tests for weighted increments, and an e2e scenario that exercises an autorollback on a synthetic semantic-regression. See commits for details.

review_comments: Rajesh Patel: Overall looks good. A few questions: (1) can you walk through how probe failures correlate with production errors to avoid double-counting?; (2) what's the expected perf cost of running probes at scale?

Samantha Lee (author): Reply: probes are treated as auxiliary checks and must meet quorum with production checks before rollback. Perf cost is bounded by rate limits and a shared worker pool; added default rate limit of 100 probes/min per region and a circuit breaker that pauses probes if API error rate crosses 5%.
Noah Kim: Can we expose a rollout-level metric that surfaces probe quorum pass rate? This would make incident triage much faster.
Samantha Lee: Added rollout.probe_quorum_pass_ratio gauge in this PR and wired to the dashboard. See observability/dashboards/rollouts-probing.json and pkg/metrics/ingest.go for labels.
Ethan Zhao: Minor - prefer explicit backoff for probe retries instead of exponential (we want deterministic probe timing). Also add unit tests for quorum calculation.
Samantha Lee: Switched to deterministic linear backoff and added quorum unit tests + integration assertion in e2e.
Rajesh Patel: Approve after address of probe CPU isolation comment.
Samantha Lee: Added CPU limits and requests for probe pods; moved probe runner to dedicated worker queue. Updated docs to call out resource sizing guidance.
